candidates.source_name: ERAR (KPK) — aplikacija za prikaz porabe javnega denarja
candidates.why_relevant: Successor to Supervizor, run by the Commission for the Prevention of Corruption (KPK). Exposes actual transactions from public-sector bodies (ministries, Banka Slovenije-adjacent bodies, municipalities, state-owned companies) to named legal entities. Bottom-up way to discover which payment processors, card personalisation firms, ATM service providers and core-banking integrators are actually paid by Slovenian public bodies, including where the original tender notice is hard to find. Vendor names harvested here become the seeds for downstream source discovery.
candidates.access_status: public, free, no login for core transaction search
candidates.legal_status: public information of public character under ZIntPK arts. 75.a/75.b; OPSI metadata record lists CC BY 4.0
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/scripted vendor-name lookups (payee search) for a curated list of payments/banking vendors; monthly re-pull. Prefer the OPSI-registered dataset record as the entry point and respect robots.txt/rate limits; escalate to a KPK data request if bulk export is needed.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query (sl) + OPSI dataset record cross-check

brief: Slovenia's contract-and-payment transparency layer is unusually well developed and splits cleanly into three tiers: ERAR (KPK, successor to Supervizor, rebuilt 2023-24, CC BY 4.0, monthly) exposes actual public-sector transactions to named payees; the procurement tier (enarocanje.si contract publication, the OPSI datasets Evidenca JN / odločitve o oddaji / objavljene pogodbe, and the STATIST analytics app with CSV export covering all awards since 2013) carries notices, award decisions and signed contracts; and since 1 January 2023 the UJP JN Plačila system adds statutory monthly reporting of executed payments above EUR 40,000 back onto the contract record — a near-unique contract-to-cash trail. AJPES is not a contract register despite the seed hypothesis; it is the entity-resolution and financials layer (ePRS, JOLP, eRTR, RDL) that turns a payee string into an identified, sized company, and its RDL access appears to have been restricted since August 2025. The main obstacles are technical and legal rather than availability: ERAR is a client-rendered SPA with no documented API, the OPSI contracts record carries stale metadata and an undefined licence, and no banking/payments CPV filter has yet been built. Recommended next steps are probing ERAR's XHR endpoints, resolving the Slovenian OCDS endpoint, and testing the public-sector e-invoice dataset, which would be the finest-grained vendor spend signal in the cell.
